_about: Retrieval eval for the recipe corpus. Relevance is by DOCUMENT ID (a doc's recipe_name), not by keyword substring: the old proxy counted a chunk relevant if it contained a word like 'chicken', which structurally favoured BM25 and hit a ceiling because common words appear in a large fraction of 3,090 documents. Each query here is phrased to describe a dish WITHOUT using words from its title, so a retriever cannot win by lexical overlap alone.
_caveat: Gold sets are built by an explicit, restatable rule, not by opinion: for each query, every corpus recipe whose NAME identifies the dish (e.g. contains 'quiche', 'slaw', 'smoothie'), minus names where the dish is only a component of a different main ('Fish Tacos with Mango Slaw') or a different dish sharing the word ('Corn Bread Dressing', 'Enchilada Meatballs'). This replaced a hand-picked 1-3 IDs per query, which was badly incomplete and systematically understated every retriever: 'blended cold fruit drink' listed one smoothie while the corpus holds 41, so a retriever returning a different perfectly good smoothie scored zero. Labels went 56 -> 249 and absolute scores rose accordingly, so numbers from before 2026-08-13 are NOT comparable to numbers after. Still not a domain-reviewed gold standard: the rule keys on the title, so a dish that matches the query but is titled obliquely is still unlabelled. Read A/B differences between configs together with the bootstrap CI, not absolute values.

_fields.query: the user query sent to the retriever
_fields.expects: legacy keyword proxy, used only when relevant_ids is absent
_fields.match_all: legacy; require ALL keyword terms (default false)
